title: Warm Crunchy Moroccan Lamb Mrouzia
description: A hearty, crunchy Moroccan-inspired brunch dish featuring lamb, spices, and fresh herbs, all wrapped up in a crispy pastry pocket. Perfect for a weekend morning or a special occasion.

ingredients.name: 1 pound boneless lamb shoulder, thinly sliced

instructions: In a large bowl, combine the flour, salt, and cold butter. Use a pastry blender or your fingers to work the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add the egg and mix until the dough comes together in a ball.
Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out the dough to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Transfer the dough to a lazy Susan spinner or a large plate.
In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic and cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is softened and lightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the cumin, coriander, cinnamon, turmeric, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the lamb and cook, stirring occasionally, until it is browned and cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the parsley and cilantro.
To assemble the mrouzia, place a tablespoon or two of the lamb mixture onto one half of the dough circle.
Brush the edges of the dough with a little water, then fold the other half of the dough over the filling to form a half-moon shape.
Use a knife or pastry brush to create a decorative edge around the mrouzia.
Brush the tops of the mrouzia with a little egg wash and bake until golden brown, about 20-25 minutes.
